name: sendgrid-mcp
description: SendGrid (messaging): me, send. Every tool maps to a documented endpoint.

platform_mcp_sendgrid_api_key.title: PLATFORM_MCP_SENDGRID_API_KEY
platform_mcp_sendgrid_api_key.description: SendGrid API key with Mail Send (and, for `me`, User Account read) permission, sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <API key>' ('add an HTTP Authorization header to your API request that contains an API Key', https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/how-to-use-the-sendgrid-v3-api/authentication). EU-pinned accounts live on https://api.eu.sendgrid.com, which this server does not switch to.

platform_mcp_sendgrid_sender.title: PLATFORM_MCP_SENDGRID_SENDER
platform_mcp_sendgrid_sender.description: Verified sender address used as `from.email` on every send ('from (object with required email field)' — a verified Sender Identity or authenticated domain is required, https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/mail-send/mail-send). Env: PLATFORM_MCP_SENDGRID_SENDER.

platform_mcp_sendgrid_env.title: PLATFORM_MCP_SENDGRID_ENV
platform_mcp_sendgrid_env.description: Vendor environment (default production): sandbox = production host with test accounts or test keys. Credentials are the environment's own; see adapter.environments in the catalog entry.

platform_mcp_sendgrid_base_url.title: PLATFORM_MCP_SENDGRID_BASE_URL
platform_mcp_sendgrid_base_url.description: Optional https base URL override (a mock or a private gateway); replaces the selected environment's base_url. Never echoed in errors.

tools.name: me
tools.description: GET /v3/user/account answers {type: 'free' | 'paid' ('The type of account for this user'), reputation ('The sender reputation for this user')}; there is no richer identity endpoint on the API key itself.

tools.name: send
tools.description: Sends one plain-text email: `to` is one recipient address (personalizations[0].to[0].email — 'personalizations: An array of messages and their metadata', 'to: array of recipient objects with required email field'), `from.email` comes from the per-install `sender` config field, `subject` is required by SendGrid (a missing subject is a 400 -> isError), `text` is content[0] with type text/plain; `channel` is ignored. SendGrid answers '202 Accepted' with an empty body, so status is the literal 'accepted' and message_id is empty (the id is only in the X-Message-Id response header, which the runtime does not expose).
